newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Marco Polo sees stiff hotel competition.
newsitem.headline: Marco Polo sees stiff hotel competition.

text.p: Hotel and property company Marco Polo Developments Ltd said on Monday its Singapore hotel is expected to face keen competition due to slower visitor growth and new hotels and food and beverage outlets.

"The Marco Polo, Singapore is expected to face very competitive market conditions during the current financial year," it said in a statement accompanying its financial results for year ended March 31, 1997.
Last year, revenue and operating profit from its Singapore hotel unit declined marginally due to the additional supplies of rooms in the local industry and decrease in visitor arrivals.
The group saw a 12.9 percent growth in net profit to Singapore $18.27 million for financial year ended March 31, 1997.
It attributed the growth to lower than expected costs of the Parc Oasis residential development, improved rental income and the write-back of overprovision for property tax on Wheelock Place.
The group however reported a sharp 49 percent drop in turnover to S$77.22 million due mainly to lower revenue from the completion of the Parc Oasis development.

Marco Polo expects to fully let its first and second floor of Wheelock Place along Orchard Road, Singapore's main shopping belt, by the end of 1997 and added the renewals of the office leases will generate good growth.
Marco Polo said some profit are likely to be recognised this financial year from its new Ardmore Park condominium, where construction works are scheduled to start in August 1997.
